title: The Web Starts at CERN
paragraphs: In nineteen eighty nine, a young scientist named Tim Berners-Lee worked at CERN, a big research centre in Switzerland. Many scientists there had documents on different computers, and sharing them was slow. So he wrote a proposal for a better way to connect information. He wanted everyone to find information easily.

By the end of nineteen ninety, the first Web server and the first browser were working at CERN. The first website was kept on Berners-Lee's own computer, and it explained the project itself. At first, mostly scientists used it.

In nineteen ninety three, CERN said that anyone could use the Web software for free. This decision helped the Web spread quickly around the world. Today, billions of people use it every day. People can now read news, watch films and talk with friends online.
